units.expected: The statement that these factors "could significantly increase our payment obligations" under the pension plans now reads "could increase our payment obligations", and the liability-driven investment strategy sentence moves from the middle to the end of the paragraph.

Tariffs and retaliatory counter measures are elevated into the headline, and the body adds proposed additional export controls and tariffs, limited access to rare earth minerals and other raw materials, tariff-driven cost, pricing, market access and planning impacts, and the cost and fines exposure of complying with rapidly changing trade restrictions, while dropping the limitation of sanctions to parties in certain conflict zones.

The PFAS manufacturing exit moves from in progress ("is progressing toward the exit of all PFAS manufacturing by the end of 2025") to completed ("completed its exit of PFAS manufacturing at the end of 2025"), with new disclosure of ongoing water treatment, remediation and facility disposition obligations, third-party PFAS product use that will continue beyond 2025 with transitions not completed, the dropped 2018 State of Minnesota settlement example ($897 million pre-tax charge), and asset retirement obligations broadened to charges on ongoing asset use, retirement or disposition.

The paragraph on artificial intelligence development, use and regulatory risk is removed and replaced by a new paragraph on risks as a direct and indirect supplier to the U.S. and other governments, covering procurement compliance, audit and contract termination rights, funding uncertainty, False Claims Act liability and suspension or debarment, with customers added to the parties whose conduct creates compliance risk.

Adds a new passage on tariffs and other trade restrictions raising imported raw material and component costs, disrupting supply chains, limiting access to end markets, lowering profitability and clouding long-term planning, and narrows the PFAS customer-preference reference to products without third-party manufactured PFAS.

Military conflicts are dropped as a named example of events that could interrupt or terminate supplier relationships and are replaced by a pointer to the disruptive events in the first risk factor (which now covers tariffs and trade restrictions), alongside minor wording changes ("shortage" to "shortages", "interrupted or terminated").

New risk factor on the Company's use of artificial intelligence, covering inaccurate or biased outputs, third-party AI vendor dependence, leakage of confidential or third-party data into AI systems, evolving AI regulation, competitive pressure, and resulting legal, regulatory and reputational harm.

The description of the structural reorganization (shrinking the corporate center, simplifying the supply chain, streamlining the geographic footprint, removing management layers, realigning go-to-market models and cutting manufacturing roles to match production volumes) is deleted and replaced with a general statement that workforce restructuring is expected to deliver benefits but also affects business groups, functions and geographies.

The S&P Global Ratings outlook on 3M's BBB+ credit rating changes from negative to stable, while the Moody's A3 stable and Fitch A- stable ratings are unchanged and "Fitch" is renamed "Fitch Ratings".
The risk that consents or approvals required for the Solventum separation will not be obtained, or will be obtained subject to material modifications to the underlying arrangements, is deleted.

New section authorizes subscription-line borrowing secured by Unfunded Commitments, capped at the lesser of 25% of aggregate Commitments and aggregate Unfunded Commitments with each borrowing repaid within 364 days, requires LP lender confirmations, runs the preferred return from the borrowing date and requires IRR reporting with and without the facility.

General Partner catch-up in clause (c) changed from 100% to the General Partner to 80% to the General Partner and 20% to the Limited Partner, still until the General Partner has received 20%; the 8% preferred return and final 80/20 split are unchanged.
Post-Commitment Period Management Fee rate reduced from 1.50% to 1.25% of Net Invested Capital; the 2.00% of Commitments rate during the Commitment Period is unchanged.

Tax Distributions section deleted, eliminating the General Partner's authority to make annual tax distributions at the Assumed Tax Rate (New York, New York individual rate) as advances against Section 3.1 distributions.

Added sentence makes the Partnership bear its allocable share of the regulatory compliance costs of the Manager and the General Partner (Form PF and Form ADV filings, regulatory examinations), which were not a Partnership Expense before; the $2,000,000 organizational expense cap is unchanged.

Approval of Affiliated Transactions moved from prior approval by the Advisory Committee to advance approval by the General Partner as fair and reasonable, with only written notice to the Advisory Committee.
Suspension of the Commitment Period on a Key Person Event changed from discretionary ("may suspend") to mandatory ("shall suspend"); the two-of-three trigger and 180 day cure are unchanged.

New section permits sales of Investments to a Manager-affiliated Continuation Vehicle only with prior Advisory Committee approval, a competitive process supported by a fairness opinion, and a cash-or-roll election for each Limited Partner on at least 20 Business Days' notice, with fee disclosure and expenses borne by the vehicle.

Carve-out added to the exclusion for proceedings a Covered Person initiates against the Partnership or another Covered Person, so proceedings a Covered Person brings to enforce its rights under Section 6.1 (exculpation and indemnification) are now indemnified.
Deadline for delivering annual audited financial statements extended from 90 days to 120 days after fiscal year end; the 60 day quarterly reporting deadline is unchanged.
